speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs whether increased law enforcement operations will be undertaken at Orchard Towers so as to reduce or deter any illegal or vice activities there or around its vicinity.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) in the past three years, how many Police reports have been made on crime and vice activities at Orchard Towers; (b) what enforcement actions have been taken by the Police; and (c) what plans do the Police have to eradicate crime and vice activities at Orchard Towers.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This number has decreased in the past three years, as the Police have actively managed the licences they grant, to take into consideration the Urban Redevelopment Authority's (URA's) planning intent, feedback from the community and the prevailing law and order situation.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Police have been taking enforcement action against unlicensed massage establishments at Orchard Towers, and the number has remained stable over the past three years.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Five operators have been dealt with, of which four were fined, and one was issued a stern warning.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Police will continue its enforcement efforts in this area.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Police have deployed more resources there, including Special Operations Command troops.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: This enhanced presence is supplemented with an increased deployment of closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras to deter street-walking and other illegal activities.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Police have also maintained a strong tempo of enforcement operations.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: These operations were on top of the Police’s regular checks.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Police will continue to keep a close watch on the law and order situation at Orchard Towers and ensure the safety of the public.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Last Saturday, I visited Orchard Towers with my grassroots leaders and officers from the Police, the National Environment Agency and the Land Transport Authority.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I understand that there are currently more than 30 public entertainment outlets within Orchard Towers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can I request that the Ministry consider setting a cap on the number of public entertainment outlets within one property development, especially within a mixed development comprising many residential units?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I would also like to ask the Police to consider not renewing some of the Public Entertainment Licences at Orchard Towers when they are up for renewal, especially for those with poor public order records.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: During my walkabout at Orchard Towers, we saw a number of beauty salons there.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: From the look of the shopfront, I would be suspicious of the sort of treatments they provide.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While I am glad to hear from the Senior Parliamentary Secretary that the Police have taken action against massage establishments, those with licences, at Orchard Towers, I believe the Police have also stopped issuing massage establishment licences there.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I understand that these beauty salons do not require any licence to operate.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I would, therefore, like to ask if the Police are taking any actions against these beauty salons to ensure that they do not circumvent the licensing regime and engage in vice activities.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Given these considerations, the Police are unlikely to grant new Public Entertainment Licences for Orchard Towers.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Police conduct regular checks on the Public Entertainment Licensees to ensure that they comply with all licensing conditions.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Licencees with infringements of licensing conditions may have their licence not renewed upon expiry.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: For those with more egregious infringements, their licences may even be suspended or cancelled by the licensing officer.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The Police also conduct regular enforcement to ensure that operators do not circumvent the licensing regime and engage in vice activities.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: It is an offence for beauty salons, as the Member mentioned, to provide massage services without a licence under the Massage Establishments Act.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: An operator may be liable to a maximum fine of $10,000 or two years, or both.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: If vice activities are detected, the operator may be liable for additional vice-related offences under the Women's Charter.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It creates an unsafe and uncomfortable environment for people who just want to have a decent meal in the buildings that surround Orchard Towers.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, could MHA prioritise anti-vice raids on Orchard Towers to clean up that strip of Orchard Road?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: There is also an investigation into an alleged murder there.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And I think this brings to bear the urgency of the task.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am just wondering, if we stepped up enforcement in Orchard Towers, are we really addressing the root of the problem?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And we are just spending our resources just chasing our tail.
